#!/bin/sh
# Start a sandbox test run of agent/ (public data, never ranked), follow it to the end and record its score in
# experiments/runs.jsonl (commit that file afterwards). Usage, from anywhere: dev/test-run.sh <version> ["note"] [experiment]
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
version=${1:?usage: dev/test-run.sh <version> [note] [experiment]}
note=${2:-}
experiment=${3:-}
commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
dirty=no; [ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- agent)" ] && dirty=yes
log=$(mktemp)
record="python3 dev/track.py platform RUN --version '$version' --experiment '$experiment' --note '$note' --commit $commit --dirty $dirty"
trap 'run=$(grep -o "run_[0-9a-f]*" "$log" | head -1); echo; echo "Stopped following; the run goes on. Record it once it ends:"; echo "  $record" | sed "s/RUN/${run:-<run id>}/"; exit 130' INT
atira test-run ./agent --no-open --follow </dev/null | tee "$log"
run=$(grep -o 'run_[0-9a-f]*' "$log" | head -1)
rm -f "$log"
[ -n "$run" ] || { echo "No run id in the output; record it later with: $record"; exit 1; }
eval "$(echo "$record" | sed "s/RUN/$run/")" && python3 dev/track.py report

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
One turn of the improve-and-measure loop on our own evals: name the agent as it stands, run it on the evals of
dev/train_rules.json, download every run's timed log, turn the scores into one reward by the rule in that file and
say whether this version beats the best so far.

    python3 dev/trainloop.py step "what changed"          # package agent/, run, wait, download, judge
    python3 dev/trainloop.py step "..." --evals a,b --repeats 2 --package submission
    python3 dev/trainloop.py adopt eve_... "note"         # judge an eval entry that already ran (no new runs)
    python3 dev/trainloop.py collect <version>            # finish a step whose wait was interrupted
    python3 dev/trainloop.py report                       # every version, best first

A version is named <prefix>-<date>-<time>-<zone> on the Central European clock (CET in winter, CEST in summer), and
its eval runs carry that name on the platform. Everything of a version is kept in experiments/train/<version>/
(gitignored): the package that ran, the rules, and per run its score and its log with the run's clock on every line.
experiments/train/ledger.jsonl holds one line per version.

The loop only measures. What to change between two steps is decided by reading the logs of the runs that lost
points, and the change has to be general: nothing seen on an eval's sites (values, labels, addresses) may go into
agent/. Each step costs evals x repeats of the team's eval runs (12 an hour, shared).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import zoneinfo
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
RULES = ROOT / "dev" / "train_rules.json"
TRAIN = ROOT / "experiments" / "train"
LEDGER = TRAIN / "ledger.jsonl"
WAITING = ("queued", "provisioning", "setup", "running", "starting", "pending")


def atira(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    done = subprocess.run(["atira", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    if check and done.returncode:
        raise SystemExit(f"atira {' '.join(args)} failed: {(done.stderr or done.stdout).strip()[:400]}")
    return done.stdout


def git(*args: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()


def rules() -> dict:
    return json.loads(RULES.read_text())


def new_version(prefix: str) -> str:
    now = datetime.datetime.now(zoneinfo.ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin"))
    name = f"{prefix}-{now:%Y%m%d-%H%M}-{now:%Z}"
    return name if not (TRAIN / name).exists() else f"{prefix}-{now:%Y%m%d-%H%M%S}-{now:%Z}"


def ledger() -> list[dict]:
    """One record per version: a later line of the same version replaces the earlier one."""
    if not LEDGER.exists():
        return []
    latest: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for line in LEDGER.read_text().splitlines():
        if line.strip():
            record = json.loads(line)
            latest[record["version"]] = record
    return list(latest.values())


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the rule and the reward


def run_reward(run: dict, rule: dict) -> float:
    """A scored run's reward: its quality (the rule's `not_eligible` when it is not eligible) plus the rule's
    weight on cost x time, with the platform's floors ($0.01, 1 s)."""
    quality = run["quality"] if run["eligible"] else rule["not_eligible"]
    cost_x_time = max(run["cost_usd"], 0.01) * max(run["seconds"], 1.0)
    return rule["quality"] * quality + rule["cost_x_time"] * cost_x_time


def judge(record: dict, earlier: list[dict], rule: dict) -> dict:
    """Fill in a version's reward and its verdict against the best complete version before it."""
    per_eval = []
    for entry in record["evals"].values():
        counted = [r for r in entry["runs"] if r["counted"]]
        for r in counted:
            r["reward"] = round(run_reward(r, rule["reward"]), 2)
        entry["reward"] = round(sum(r["reward"] for r in counted) / len(counted), 2) if counted else None
        per_eval.append(entry["reward"])
    record["complete"] = bool(per_eval) and all(value is not None for value in per_eval)
    record["reward"] = round(sum(per_eval) / len(per_eval), 2) if record["complete"] else None
    same = [r for r in earlier if r.get("complete") and sorted(r["evals"]) == sorted(record["evals"])]
    best = max(same, key=lambda r: r["reward"], default=None)
    record["best_before"] = best and {"version": best["version"], "reward": best["reward"]}
    if not record["complete"]:
        record["verdict"] = "incomplete"
    elif best is None:
        record["verdict"] = "first"
    else:
        gain = record["reward"] - best["reward"]
        record["verdict"] = "better" if gain >= rule["min_gain"] else "worse" if gain <= -rule["min_gain"] else "same"
        record["gain"] = round(gain, 2)
    return record


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- runs on the platform


def entry_of(slug: str, entry_id: str) -> dict | None:
    entries = json.loads(atira("eval", "runs", slug, "--json")).get("entries", [])
    return next((e for e in entries if e["id"] == entry_id), None)


def wait(slugs: dict[str, str], repeats: int, minutes: float) -> None:
    """Until every entry has its scored runs, or nothing of it is waiting or running any more. The platform starts a
    run again when it failed one itself, a little after the failure, so an idle entry is looked at twice."""
    deadline, idle = time.time() + minutes * 60, 0
    while time.time() < deadline:
        open_runs, lines = 0, []
        for slug, entry_id in slugs.items():
            runs = (entry_of(slug, entry_id) or {}).get("runs", [])
            scored = sum(r["status"] == "scored" for r in runs)
            busy = sum(r["status"] in WAITING for r in runs)
            if scored < repeats and (busy or not runs):
                open_runs += 1
            lines.append(f"{slug}: {scored}/{repeats} scored, {busy} waiting or running")
        print(time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), "; ".join(lines), flush=True)
        if not open_runs:
            idle += 1
            if idle >= 2:
                return
        else:
            idle = 0
        time.sleep(30)
    print(f"Still running after {minutes:.0f} min; finish later with: python3 dev/trainloop.py collect <version>")


def download(version: str, slug: str, entry_id: str) -> dict:
    """An entry's runs with their scores, and each run's status and timed log in the version's folder."""
    entry = entry_of(slug, entry_id) or {"runs": []}
    folder = TRAIN / version / slug
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    runs = []
    for run in entry["runs"]:
        run_id = run["run_id"]
        (folder / f"{run_id}.json").write_text(atira("status", run_id, "--json", check=False))
        (folder / f"{run_id}.log").write_text(atira("logs", run_id, check=False))  # every line starts with its time
        counted = run["status"] == "scored"
        runs.append({"run_id": run_id, "status": run["status"], "counted": counted, "error": run.get("error"),
                     "quality": run.get("quality"), "eligible": bool(run.get("eligible")),
                     "cost_usd": (run.get("cost_micro_usd") or 0) / 1e6, "seconds": (run.get("duration_ms") or 0) / 1e3,
                     "log": str((folder / f"{run_id}.log").relative_to(ROOT))})
    return {"entry": entry_id, "eval_version": entry.get("version_id"), "runs": runs}


def finish(record: dict) -> int:
    """Download, judge, write the ledger line and print the verdict."""
    rule = json.loads((TRAIN / record["version"] / "rules.json").read_text())
    for slug, entry in record["evals"].items():
        record["evals"][slug] = download(record["version"], slug, entry["entry"])
    earlier = [r for r in ledger() if r["version"] != record["version"]]
    judge(record, earlier, rule)
    with LEDGER.open("a") as out:
        out.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"\n{record['version']}: {record['note']}")
    for slug, entry in record["evals"].items():
        for run in entry["runs"]:
            what = (f"quality {run['quality']}, ${run['cost_usd']:.4f}, {run['seconds']:.0f} s, reward {run['reward']}"
                    if run["counted"] else f"not counted ({run['status']}: {run['error']})")
            print(f"  {slug} {run['run_id']}: {what}\n    log {run['log']}  page https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/"
                  f"{run['run_id']}")
    best = record["best_before"]
    against = f" against {best['reward']} of {best['version']}" if best else ""
    print(f"reward {record['reward']}{against}: {record['verdict'].upper()}")
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- commands


def package(version: str, source: str) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    """What the runs get: a folder with the tracked files of agent/ as they are now, or a platform package id."""
    if source:
        return source, {"package": source}
    folder = TRAIN / version / "package"
    for name in git("ls-files", "agent").splitlines():
        target = folder / name
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(ROOT / name, target)
    return str(folder / "agent"), {"package": "agent/", "commit": git("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"),
                                   "branch": git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"),
                                   "changed": git("status", "--porcelain", "--", "agent").splitlines()}


def cmd_step(args) -> int:
    rule = rules()
    slugs = args.evals.split(",") if args.evals else rule["evals"]
    repeats = args.repeats or rule["repeats"]
    version = new_version(args.prefix)
    (TRAIN / version).mkdir(parents=True)
    (TRAIN / version / "rules.json").write_text(json.dumps(rule, indent=1))
    what, origin = package(version, args.package)
    record = {"version": version, "at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()), "note": args.note,
              "repeats": repeats, **origin, "evals": {}}
    for slug in slugs:
        out = atira("eval", "run", slug, "--package", what, "--repeats", str(repeats), "--label", version)
        entry = re.search(r"eve_[0-9a-f]+", out)
        if not entry:
            raise SystemExit(f"No entry id in the answer for {slug}: {out[:300]}")
        record["evals"][slug] = {"entry": entry[0]}
        print(f"{version}: {slug} -> {entry[0]} ({repeats} run{'s' if repeats > 1 else ''})", flush=True)
    (TRAIN / version / "step.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=1))
    wait({slug: e["entry"] for slug, e in record["evals"].items()}, repeats, args.minutes)
    return finish(record)


def cmd_adopt(args) -> int:
    rule = rules()
    found = None
    for slug in (args.evals.split(",") if args.evals else rule["evals"]):
        entry = entry_of(slug, args.entry)
        if entry:
            found = (slug, entry)
    if not found:
        raise SystemExit(f"{args.entry} is not an entry of the evals in {RULES.name}; name its eval with --evals")
    slug, entry = found
    version = new_version(args.prefix)
    (TRAIN / version).mkdir(parents=True)
    (TRAIN / version / "rules.json").write_text(json.dumps(rule, indent=1))
    record = {"version": version, "at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
              "note": args.note or entry.get("label") or "", "repeats": entry.get("repeats", 1),
              "package": entry.get("package", {}).get("sha256", "")[:12], "adopted": entry.get("label"),
              "evals": {slug: {"entry": args.entry}}}
    (TRAIN / version / "step.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=1))
    atira("run", "name", entry["runs"][-1]["run_id"], version, check=False) if entry.get("runs") else None
    return finish(record)


def cmd_collect(args) -> int:
    step = TRAIN / args.version / "step.json"
    if not step.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"No step named {args.version} in {TRAIN.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return finish(json.loads(step.read_text()))


def cmd_report(args) -> int:
    records = sorted(ledger(), key=lambda r: (r["reward"] is None, -(r["reward"] or 0)))
    if not records:
        print("No versions yet: python3 dev/trainloop.py step \"what changed\"")
        return 0
    print(f"{'reward':>7}  {'verdict':10} {'version':32} quality / cost / seconds per counted run; note")
    for r in records:
        runs = [run for e in r["evals"].values() for run in e["runs"] if run["counted"]]
        scores = ", ".join(f"{run['quality']:g} / ${run['cost_usd']:.3f} / {run['seconds']:.0f}" for run in runs)
        reward = "-" if r["reward"] is None else f"{r['reward']:.2f}"
        print(f"{reward:>7}  {r['verdict']:10} {r['version']:32} {scores or 'no counted run'}; {r['note']}")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    step = commands.add_parser("step")
    step.add_argument("note")
    step.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=0, help="runs per eval, 1 to 3 (default: the rules file's)")
    step.add_argument("--package", default="", help="submission, test, sub_..., run_... (default: agent/ as it is)")
    step.add_argument("--minutes", type=float, default=45, help="how long to wait for the runs")
    adopt = commands.add_parser("adopt")
    adopt.add_argument("entry")
    adopt.add_argument("note", nargs="?", default="")
    collect = commands.add_parser("collect")
    collect.add_argument("version")
    commands.add_parser("report")
    for command in (step, adopt):
        command.add_argument("--evals", default="", help="eval slugs, comma-separated (default: the rules file's)")
        command.add_argument("--prefix", default="train", help="what the version name starts with")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    return {"step": cmd_step, "adopt": cmd_adopt, "collect": cmd_collect, "report": cmd_report}[args.command](args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
One turn of the improve-and-measure loop on our own evals: name the agent as it stands, run it on the evals of
dev/train_rules.json, download every run's timed log, turn the scores into one reward by the rule in that file and
say whether this version beats the best so far.

    python3 dev/trainloop.py step "what changed"          # package agent/, run, wait, download, judge
    python3 dev/trainloop.py step "..." --evals a,b --repeats 2 --package submission
    python3 dev/trainloop.py adopt eve_... "note"         # judge an eval entry that already ran (no new runs)
    python3 dev/trainloop.py collect <version>            # finish a step whose wait was interrupted
    python3 dev/trainloop.py report                       # every version, best first

A version is named <prefix>-<date>-<time>-<zone> on the Central European clock (CET in winter, CEST in summer), and
its eval runs carry that name on the platform. Everything of a version is kept in experiments/train/<version>/
(gitignored): the package that ran, the rules, and per run its score and its log with the run's clock on every line.
experiments/train/ledger.jsonl holds one line per version.

The loop only measures. What to change between two steps is decided by reading the logs of the runs that lost
points, and the change has to be general: nothing seen on an eval's sites (values, labels, addresses) may go into
agent/. Each step costs evals x repeats of the team's eval runs (12 an hour, shared).
"""

import datetime
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import zoneinfo
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
RULES = ROOT / "dev" / "train_rules.json"
TRAIN = ROOT / "experiments" / "train"

WAITING = ("queued", "provisioning", "setup", "running", "starting", "pending")


def atira(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    done = subprocess.run(["atira", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    if check and done.returncode:
        raise SystemExit(f"atira {' '.join(args)} failed: {(done.stderr or done.stdout).strip()[:400]}")
    return done.stdout


def git(*args: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()


def rules() -> dict:
    return json.loads(RULES.read_text())


def new_version(prefix: str) -> str:
    now = datetime.datetime.now(zoneinfo.ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin"))
    name = f"{prefix}-{now:%Y%m%d-%H%M}-{now:%Z}"
    return name if not (TRAIN / name).exists() else f"{prefix}-{now:%Y%m%d-%H%M%S}-{now:%Z}"


def ledger() -> list[dict]:
    """One record per version: a later line of the same version replaces the earlier one."""
    if not LEDGER.exists():
        return []
    latest: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for line in LEDGER.read_text().splitlines():

            latest[record["version"]] = record

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the rule and the reward


def run_reward(run: dict, rule: dict) -> float:
    """A scored run's reward: its quality (the rule's `not_eligible` when it is not eligible) plus the rule's
    weight on cost x time, with the platform's floors ($0.01, 1 s)."""
    quality = run["quality"] if run["eligible"] else rule["not_eligible"]
    cost_x_time = max(run["cost_usd"], 0.01) * max(run["seconds"], 1.0)
    return rule["quality"] * quality + rule["cost_x_time"] * cost_x_time


def judge(record: dict, earlier: list[dict], rule: dict) -> dict:
    """Fill in a version's reward and its verdict against the best complete version before it."""
    per_eval = []
    for entry in record["evals"].values():
        counted = [r for r in entry["runs"] if r["counted"]]
        for r in counted:
            r["reward"] = round(run_reward(r, rule["reward"]), 2)
        entry["reward"] = round(sum(r["reward"] for r in counted) / len(counted), 2) if counted else None
        per_eval.append(entry["reward"])
    record["complete"] = bool(per_eval) and all(value is not None for value in per_eval)
    record["reward"] = round(sum(per_eval) / len(per_eval), 2) if record["complete"] else None
    same = [r for r in earlier if r.get("complete") and sorted(r["evals"]) == sorted(record["evals"])]
    best = max(same, key=lambda r: r["reward"], default=None)
    record["best_before"] = best and {"version": best["version"], "reward": best["reward"]}
    if not record["complete"]:
        record["verdict"] = "incomplete"
    elif best is None:
        record["verdict"] = "first"
    else:
        gain = record["reward"] - best["reward"]
        record["verdict"] = "better" if gain >= rule["min_gain"] else "worse" if gain <= -rule["min_gain"] else "same"

    deadline, idle = time.time() + minutes * 60, 0
    while time.time() < deadline:

        for slug, entry_id in slugs.items():

content.text:
The loop tool is built and working: `dev/trainloop.py` with its rule in `dev/train_rules.json`. I tested it on the existing baseline run, and it is now waiting to judge the `main` and `main` + Clef runs, which the platform restarted after its model proxy failed them.

**What one step does**

```sh
python3 dev/trainloop.py step "what changed"
```

1. **Names the version** on the Central European clock, for example `train-20261011-0752-CEST`. It says CEST rather than CET because that is the zone in force today; it will say CET from the winter switch.
2. **Packages `agent/` as it stands** and runs it on the evals in the rules file, with the version name as the run label on the platform.
3. **Waits**, including for runs the platform restarts after its own failures; those failed runs are not counted.
4. **Downloads each run's timed log and score** into `experiments/train/<version>/` (gitignored), next to a copy of the package that ran.
5. **Computes the reward and a verdict** against the best earlier version: BETTER, SAME or WORSE.

**The rule**
- Reward per run = quality (0 if not eligible) − 0.01 × cost × time, using the platform's floors.
- A version's reward is the mean over its evals.
- A version only counts as better or worse if the reward moves by at least 1 point.
- All of that, plus the eval list and repeats, is editable in `dev/train_rules.json`.

**First result**
The current submission on your portal: quality 10, $0.16, 699 s, reward 8.85, recorded as the first baseline. `python3 dev/trainloop.py report` lists every version, best first.

**What it does not do**
- **It measures; it doesn't change the agent.** Deciding what to change between steps is still a person's or my job, by reading the downloaded logs. The fair-play rules apply there: a fix must be general, and nothing seen on the eval sites may go into `agent/`.
- **Each step spends eval runs.** A step costs evals × repeats runs out of the team's shared 12 per hour, so with one eval and one repeat you get at most 12 steps an hour, and teammates use the same budget.
- **One run per version is noisy.** The 1-point threshold is a guess at that noise; with one eval and one repeat, treat small differences as ties.

The tool, the rules file and the `.gitignore` entry are uncommitted on branch `clef-on`, alongside the Clef change. I'll report the `main` versus `main` + Clef comparison when those two runs finish.

content.text:
That log explains the page you saw: your portals were working, and the platform took their addresses away in the middle of the run. Neither of the two train-loop runs is a valid measurement, so I stopped the local waits before they could be recorded as scores.

**What the log shows (the Clef run, started 05:59 UTC)**
- **Up to about 7 minutes in, the sites worked.** The agent was logged in and filling the bid form.
- **Then the addresses died, one site at a time.** The ERP started answering "Nothing is served here" at about 415 s, and the tender portal followed at about 484 s, mid-form.
- **The agent then wasted its remaining budget.** It retried the dead addresses dozens of times and guessed paths like `/dashboard`, `/robots.txt` and `/owncloud/`.
- **Clef did its job, and was ignored.** The `page_check` tool flagged the dead pages as errors with probability 0.99 each time, but the workers kept retrying the same address.

**The other run (plain `main`, started 05:58 UTC)**
It was handed the new addresses, but its sandbox could not connect to them at all (`ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED`), and it has been retrying the start pages for its whole run. That's why it showed only 3 model calls.

**What I can and can't say about the cause**
- The eval was not redeployed, and all four sites answer 200 at their current addresses right now, so the site code is serving.
- The platform replaced the world's public addresses between about 05:58 and 06:06 UTC. I don't know why, and the eval server's own logs aren't visible to us.
- It could be the platform rollout the organizers mentioned. It could also be a side effect of the cancellations, since `atira cancel` says it removes a run's sandbox. I can't tell from here whether my server process crashed and was restarted; the staggered site failures make a single crash less likely.

**What I'd do next**
1. Ask the organizers why an eval world's addresses change while runs are in flight; that needs fixing on their side or explaining.
2. Wait for the two broken runs to end on their own (I'm not cancelling them, in case cancelling is what triggers this), then rerun both steps with nothing else being cancelled or deployed meanwhile.
3. Separately, the dead-site retry loop is a real agent weakness this exposed: a worker should give up on a site that is gone instead of spending its whole budget on it.

Should I rerun the two steps once the current runs have ended?

content.text:
Going by the team's run log (`experiments/runs.jsonl`, 220 recorded runs), there are two different "bests" on the public dataset, and neither does well on your own evals.

**Best submission (what counts for ranking)**
`sub_63a81b12d47a68b9`, from commit `8c7ab8f` on 10 Oct at 22:17 UTC: quality 100, $0.11, 7:33. It is your current leaderboard entry (rank #7 right now) and, as the latest passing submission, your final-run candidate.

**Best run overall (never submitted)**
`run_407576f1d0cf663b`, a soak test run of `main` at commit `267427b` on 11 Oct at 04:26 UTC: quality 100, $0.097, 3:19. Its cost × time is 19, against 50 for the submission, so about 2.6 times better on the tie-breaker.

| | Commit | Quality | Cost | Time | Cost × time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Current submission | `8c7ab8f` | 100 | $0.110 | 7:33 | 50 |
| Best test run | `267427b` | 100 | $0.097 | 3:19 | 19 |
| Runner-up test run | `989a252` | 100 | $0.090 | 3:49 | 21 |

**How reliable the newer code is**
- 148 of the 201 eligible recorded runs scored 100.
- The `cost-cut-2` variant is the fastest on average (cost × time about 33) but scored 100 in only 7 of its 8 runs.
- The `cost-cut` variant scored 100 in all 10 runs, at about twice the cost × time (65).

**On your own evals, nothing is good yet**
- The current submission scored 36.3, 0, 5 and 10 on `err404-traps`, `err404-nobid`, `err404-layout` and your synth portal.
- The best eval result so far is a teammate's "coverage-and-hang-fixes" package: 100 on `err404-traps`, but 0 on `err404-nobid`, `err404-layout` and your synth portal in the same round.

So for public-1, recent `main` is clearly better than what's submitted, mainly on speed. Since the final is decided on unseen data, the eval scores are the more worrying numbers.

One caveat: that log only contains runs teammates recorded. Runs from this session (the train-loop and local ones) aren't in it.

content.text:
The local Clef run finished without a signed bid: the agent researched everything in under 8 minutes, then crashed in the bid form, so there is no agent score for this run.

The preview still shows "quality 100", but that is the expected bid I entered by hand earlier to test the adapter, not the agent's.

**What the agent got right**
All four positions had the correct material, quantity and lead time. That is a big step up from the submission's run on the same portal, which built no positions at all.

**What it got wrong**
- **Discount:** it used 0 % where the expected answer is 5 %. The mail search for the director's approval did not come back with a usable record.
- **Prices and total:** every unit price is about 5 % too high and the total is 341,171.48 against 324,113.38. That follows directly from the missing discount.
- Had it signed this answer, the eval score would have been roughly 73: reference 5, plus 52.5 for the positions (material, quantity and lead time are 70 % of the 75), with discount, prices and total lost.

**Why it crashed**
A newsletter overlay on the bid form covered the "Weiter" button. The click timed out after 5 seconds and the error was not caught, which ended the whole process. This is the same failure the team already noted for this portal in `docs/learned.md`.

**Clef and caching in this run**
- **Clef:** 16 calls, 6,460 input tokens, 18 seconds in total. It judged 11 pages as errors or dead ends and 5 as fine.
- **Cache:** 38 % of input tokens came from the cache (1.28 M of 3.39 M). That's lower than the roughly 60 % per worker seen in the sandbox, but this was a local run through your own proxy, so the two aren't directly comparable.

The two things worth fixing, both general rather than specific to this portal:

1. An overlay that intercepts a click should be closed and the click retried, and a failed click must never end the run.
2. The approval search needs to find the director's mail when records are laid out differently from public-1.

Do you want me to start with the overlay crash? It's the one that turns a roughly 73-point answer into nothing.

content.text:
Honestly: the changes made so far (Clef on, the summary lines) probably don't move the score by themselves. The evidence is one run on one portal, so treat everything below as an estimate.

**What the Clef change did in practice**
- Clef answered 16 times in about 1 second each and was right about dead pages, at 0.99 probability each time.
- The workers ignored it and kept retrying the same dead address. A correct second opinion that nobody acts on is worth nothing.
- It didn't prevent the overlay crash or find the missing discount mail.
- So I'd expect Clef as wired today to add a little cost and no points. It would only start paying off if a "dead page" verdict made the worker stop or change approach.

**What we can expect, by dataset**

| Where | Today | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public-1, quality | 100 in roughly 3 of 4 runs | 148 of 201 recorded eligible runs scored 100 |
| Public-1, speed | about 3.5 min, $0.10 on recent `main` | Best soak runs; the submitted version takes 7:33 |
| Your synth portal | 0 as it stands | The one `main` + Clef run crashed before signing |
| Teammates' evals | 0 to 57, one 100 | Recorded eval runs |

**What the two fixes would be worth on your portal**
- **Overlay crash fixed:** the answer that run computed would have scored about 73 instead of nothing.
- **Approval mail found as well:** that same answer becomes 100, since the discount was the only thing wrong.

That is for this one seed. Other seeds use different layouts and rule traps, so I'd expect a spread, not a uniform 100.

**For the final run**
The organizers said most teams dropped on the private dataset, and your eval scores say the same would happen to the current submission. I can't put a number on the private score. What I can say is that fixing general failures, the kind your portals expose, is the only work that raises it, and that Clef and caching tweaks are not where the points are.

One decision for the team, separate from all this: recent `main` is about 2.6 times better than the current submission on cost × time at the same public quality. Submitting it would improve the public rank, but it also replaces the final candidate, so it's worth confirming how it does on the evals first.

import json
rows={}
for l in open("experiments/runs.jsonl"):
    l=l.strip()
    if l:
        try: r=json.loads(l); rows[r["id"]]=r
        except ValueError: pass
def P(r): return r.get("platform") or {}
ok=[r for r in rows.values() if P(r).get("quality")==100 and P(r).get("eligible")]
def secs(r): return P(r).get("scored_duration_s") or r.get("duration_s") or 0
def cost(r): return P(r).get("cost_usd") or 0
print("fastest quality-100 runs:")
for r in sorted(ok,key=secs)[:10]:
    print(f"  {secs(r):5.0f}s ${cost(r):.4f} cxt {max(cost(r),.01)*secs(r):5.1f} req {r.get('requests')} in {r.get('input_tokens')} out {r.get('output_tokens')} {r['id']} {r.get('version')}/{r.get('experiment')} {r.get('commit')} {r.get('started_at','')[5:16]}")
print("cheapest quality-100 runs:")
for r in sorted(ok,key=cost)[:8]:
    print(f"  {secs(r):5.0f}s ${cost(r):.4f} cxt {max(cost(r),.01)*secs(r):5.1f} req {r.get('requests')} {r['id']} {r.get('version')}/{r.get('experiment')} {r.get('commit')}")
import statistics
recent=[r for r in ok if (r.get('started_at') or '')>='2026-10-11T03']
print("recent 100s:",len(recent),"median s",statistics.median(map(secs,recent)),"median $",statistics.median(map(cost,recent)), "median requests", statistics.median([r.get('requests') or 0 for r in recent]))
EOF

content.content:
292 and 307 requests ($0.127, $0.145) for 9fb3be4, where the Q&A worker alone used 25 and 28. The 11:12 run lost
  its time to model stalls (a 180 s reader timeout delayed the positions to 262 s, the tender watch fired, and
  verify timed out), not to the Q&A.
- Cost per caller (llm.USAGE, printed after the run summary): Qwen bills uncached input $0.15/M, cached input about
  $0.016/M (cache blocks of 1568 tokens; most calls only reuse the system prompt block) and output $0.47/M. Baseline
  run_92294f32 ($0.145, 297 calls): mail search workers 26 %, ERP detail workers 21 %, ERP/spec readers 11 %, spec
  attempts 9 %, tender workers 7 %, mail readers 6 %. Step count times view size is the lever, not caching.
- Time cuts (cost-cut): the mail planner waited 45 s for tender keys that arrive at ~120 s, so every run planned from
  the brief alone 45 s late; no wait now. verify_board (18-47 s) runs beside the first answer. Six mail tabs instead
  of four. Seven test runs, all 100: 264-381 s against 375-533 s before.
- Mail search with thinking off took 211 calls instead of 85 and lost end_reserves in one run: keep thinking on.
- ERP hits whose rows contradict the requirement are read only when needed (ERP_DEFER_REST): detail calls 28-32
  instead of 36-53, $0.112-0.129 per run. Records that finished after a requirement's choice were never used anyway.
- cost-cut-2: compact ERP views (gate pages, repeated views, the record banner and tab bars once) halved the
  material reader's text with the same records (8/8 offline); later bid positions entered by the model's mapping
  cut the form worker to 5 calls. The first group search the model makes is repeated for the other groups
  (AGENT_ERP_BATCH): ERP search calls 20-22 -> 4. Detail workers end once open_pages finds no link of their record
  left (ERP_DETAIL_STOP): detail calls 29-39 -> 22-27. Test runs of 4f94f35: 100, 100, 100 at $0.086-0.103.
- Mail search and mail readers are now about half the cost (42-55 %); the next cuts are there.
- A record-level number format comes from a model and does not bind every figure: a soak run (80.1) read an FX
  fixing tagged "de" whose rate was written with a decimal point, parsed it as ten thousand times the rate and bid
  three USD positions at millions of EUR. A separator that cannot group thousands is now the decimal mark, and a
  base price more than 100x (or under 1/1000) its ERP per-piece price is blanked and sends FX to the gap pass.
- Cheaper own-key models on OpenRouter (model-qwen3.7-flash, model-gpt-oss-120b): neither keeps quality. Qwen3.7
  Flash (only Alibaba serves it; not Fireworks) scored 21.7, 59.9 and 72 in 10-16 min for $0.039-0.051; its
  thinking-off tender worker re-requested the TAN instead of submitting, so two runs looped through TAN requests
  until the deadline, and research missed the discount, total and metal index window. GPT-OSS-120B (DeepInfra)
  scored 10: no positions by the answer deadline, thinking-on calls hit the 180 s timeout. Hosted Qwen stays.
- OpenRouter reasoning for Qwen: {"effort": "low", "exclude": true} still bills 2,000-4,000 hidden reasoning tokens
  per call (23-43 s); {"enabled": false} gives 0. Qwen3.7 Flash prices triple above 32k prompt tokens.

  $0.016/M (cache blocks of 1568 tokens; most calls only reuse the system prompt block) and output $0.47/M. Baseline
  run_92294f32 ($0.145, 297 calls): mail search workers 26 %, ERP detail workers 21 %, ERP/spec readers 11 %, spec
  attempts 9 %, tender workers 7 %, mail readers 6 %. Step count times view size is the lever, not caching.
- Time cuts (cost-cut): the mail planner waited 45 s for tender keys that arrive at ~120 s, so every run planned from
  the brief alone 45 s late; no wait now. verify_board (18-47 s) runs beside the first answer. Six mail tabs instead
  of four. Seven test runs, all 100: 264-381 s against 375-533 s before.
- Mail search with thinking off took 211 calls instead of 85 and lost end_reserves in one run: keep thinking on.
- ERP hits whose rows contradict the requirement are read only when needed (ERP_DEFER_REST): detail calls 28-32
  instead of 36-53, $0.112-0.129 per run. Records that finished after a requirement's choice were never used anyway.
- cost-cut-2: compact ERP views (gate pages, repeated views, the record banner and tab bars once) halved the
  material reader's text with the same records (8/8 offline); later bid positions entered by the model's mapping
  cut the form worker to 5 calls. The first group search the model makes is repeated for the other groups
  (AGENT_ERP_BATCH): ERP search calls 20-22 -> 4. Detail workers end once open_pages finds no link of their record
  left (ERP_DETAIL_STOP): detail calls 29-39 -> 22-27. Test runs of 4f94f35: 100, 100, 100 at $0.086-0.103.
- Mail search and mail readers are now about half the cost (42-55 %); the next cuts are there.
- A record-level number format comes from a model and does not bind every figure: a soak run (80.1) read an FX
  fixing tagged "de" whose rate was written with a decimal point, parsed it as ten thousand times the rate and bid
  three USD positions at millions of EUR. A separator that cannot group thousands is now the decimal mark, and a
  base price more than 100x (or under 1/1000) its ERP per-piece price is blanked and sends FX to the gap pass.

  per call (23-43 s); {"enabled": false} gives 0. Qwen3.7 Flash prices triple above 32k prompt tokens.

Read-only exploration in /Users/akshatkhair/Documents/Projects/error404ai_ehl_finals (git branch clef-on, same agent code as main). Breadth: medium. Do not edit anything.

Context: `agent/` is a pydantic-ai web agent (hosted Qwen) that researches four websites and enters a bid. We want to cut wall time and model cost of the MAIL research, which is the biggest cost. A measured good run: research finishes at ~120 s; the model-call table shows "worker mail Summary" = 90 calls, all with thinking on, 366k input tokens, 39% of run cost, and "research_mail.read_message" = 14 thinking calls, 11% of cost. Six mail tabs each run one "record kind" search at a time (approval, end_reserves, condition_rules, packaging, commitments, fx, setup_pools, project_bonus, metal_indices), each taking 26-87 s and 7-14 requests. A note in docs/learned.md says mail search with thinking off took 211 calls instead of 85 and lost a record, so thinking stays on.

Please report, with file paths and line numbers:
1. In `agent/research_mail.py` (and what it calls in `agent/orchestrator.py`, `agent/site_tools.py`, `agent/worker.py`, `agent/browser_tools.py`): the exact flow of one record-kind search. Who plans the kinds (function name), what the per-kind goal prompt is, which tools the search worker has (search, collect/collect_pages, extract, open, etc.), what a worker returns, how messages get read (`read_message`), and what budgets/limits apply (request limits, deadlines, tab count constants, env switches such as AGENT_* / MAIL_*).
2. Whether there is any existing mechanism to (a) search once for the tender reference and classify all hits for several kinds in one model call, (b) reuse a result list across kinds, (c) read several messages in one model call, (d) run a kind with thinking off. Name the functions/flags if they exist.
3. What "collect_pages" / pagination helpers do and whether their output (the list rows) is kept in the model context in full.
4. Which unit tests cover mail research (files under `agent/tests/`) and which dev scripts exercise it offline (`dev/research_check*.py` etc.), with how to run them.
5. Any comments or docs/learned.md bullets that explain why the design is one-worker-per-kind, or that warn against merging kinds (quote the lines briefly).

Also note the fair-play constraint stated in CLAUDE.md ("Must be agentic ... Rejected: a crawler/helper that gathers all evidence before model-directed investigation. Allowed helpers: parse a page the model chose, paginate a model-selected result set...") and say which of the existing helpers already rely on the "paginate a model-selected result set" allowance.

Return a concise structured report (no code dumps longer than ~15 lines each), ending with a short list of the 3-5 most promising places to cut calls or seconds, each with the function it would touch.

I'm in plan mode, so nothing is being changed. Two read-only explorations are mapping where the time and cost go (mail research, and the bid form and signing); I'll build the plan from their findings.

What the numbers already say about reaching 3rd:

- **The bar:** BaoByte in 3rd is at cost × time 3.9 ($0.033 × 1:56). Your best recorded run is 19.3.
- **2:20 alone isn't enough:** at today's cost of about $0.09, a 2:20 run comes to about 12.6, which is 4th or 5th. The run log has no 2:20 run; the fastest recorded full-score run is 3:19.
- **What 3rd needs:** for example 2:00 at $0.032, or 1:40 at $0.038. That means roughly a third of today's cost and about half the time, together.

Where a good run spends its 3:49 and $0.09:

| Phase | Wall time | Share of cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research (mail search is the long pole) | 0:00–2:00 | Mail search 39 %, mail reading 11 %, ERP and spec about 30 % |
| Filling the bid form | 2:00–3:21 | About 3 %, almost all browser time |
| Review, TAN and submit | 3:21–3:49 | Small |

So the two levers are the mail research (half the cost, and it sets when research ends) and the 80 seconds of form filling that use almost no model time.

<result>No mechanism exists today for any of (a)–(d): every kind is its own thinking-on worker run, and every kept message is its own thinking-on reader call. Everything below is from reading the code on `clef-on`; nothing was run.

## 1. Flow of one record-kind search

**Planning**
- `plan_searches()` in `agent/research_mail.py:282-330` makes one model call with thinking off (`PLAN_TIMEOUT` 30 s, retries 3) and returns a `SearchPlan` of `PlannedSearch` items.
- Each item becomes a `Kind` (name, subject, sender, sender_form, site, what, schema; `:245-254`), chosen from the nine `SCHEMAS` (`:229-242`), deduped and sorted approval-first.
- It is called from `Orchestrator._plan_mail()` (`agent/orchestrator.py:702-722`): a quick try at 30 s per call within a 75 s budget, then a patient try at `PLAN_PATIENT_TIMEOUT` 90 s.
- `Orchestrator.mails()` (`:673-700`) starts the `MAIL_TABS` sign-ins, staggered 4 s apart (`_mail_tab`, `:724`), while the plan runs.

**Scheduling**
- `Orchestrator._research_mail()` (`orchestrator.py:745-812`) queues the kinds in the order approval, end_reserves, condition_rules, then the rest.
- Each tab loops: pop a kind, then `research_mail.research_kind(session, kind, reference, deadline=, seconds=budget)`.
- The budget comes from `_kind_seconds()` (`:728-734`): mail time left divided by rounds, clamped to 120–240 s.
- A kind that stopped with nothing is re-queued once if more than `MAIL_RETRY_SECONDS` (90 s) remain (`:789-796`).
- `research_mail.research_mail()` (`research_mail.py:887-917`) is a simpler copy of this loop, used only by the dev script.

**Per-kind goal prompt**: `_goal(kind, reference, again)` at `research_mail.py:333-346`.
```
Find every message on this website that is this record, for tender {reference}: {kind.what}
- Search for the exact reference {reference} together with the word {kind.subject!r}.
- Each time a result list shows hits whose subject is this record for exactly {reference}, call keep_results
  RIGHT AWAY with those exact subjects ... Older and newer versions share a subject; keep_results keeps all.
- If the hits span several pages, call collect_pages with the ref of the list's next-page control first.
- Check every folder the mailbox has (e.g. inbox and archive) once, with the same search. ...
As soon as every folder is checked, return a one-line summary. Do not open messages yourself, do not use back()
and do not note() anything: kept messages are read for you.
```
The first prompt is this goal plus the full current view, under the generic `worker.INSTRUCTIONS` (`worker.py:25-51`).

**Search worker**: `_search()` at `research_mail.py:499-541` calls `run_worker(session, goal, Summary, deadline=until, max_steps=20, thinking=True, grounded=False, tools=(paging_tool(Collected()), keep_messages_tool(kept)))`.
- Its tools are the browser `TOOLS` (`browser_tools.py:924`: goto, click, fill, select, options, check, back, read_more, note), plus `collect_pages`, `keep_results`, and `page_check` when Clef is on (`clef.tools()`, `clef.py:146`).
- It does not have `site_tools.search/collect/extract`; `SITE_TOOLS` (`site_tools.py:740`) is not passed. The model types the query with `fill(..., submit=true)`.
- `note` stays registered even though the goal forbids it (`notes=True` is the default).
- It returns `Summary(summary: str)` (`research_tender.py:62`), which is discarded. The real output is the side effect on `kept`; `_search` returns only "done", "ended" or "stalled".
- The usage label is `"worker mail Summary"` (`worker.py:208`), which is the 90-call row in your table.

**keep_results** (`keep_messages_tool`, `research_mail.py:426-457`)
- The model passes exact link texts. The tool matches them against every link in `session.seen` (all views the tab ever showed), keeps same-host URLs, caps at 20, and opens them in parallel temporary tabs via `open_message()` (`:397-423`).
- `open_message` also opens empty reading-pane frames and retries once on a sign-in redirect.
- The tool returns only `Kept n of m` plus two header lines per message.

**Reading** (`_Reading.append`, `:460-475`; `read_message`, `:370-388`)
- Each kept view immediately spawns one `read_message` task: one model call per message, thinking on, `READ_TIMEOUT` 60 s, retries 3, output `MailRecord[kind.schema.content]`.
- An `ungrounded()` validator raises `ModelRetry`, which costs an extra call each time it fires.
- The prompt is `READ_INSTRUCTIONS` (`:349-355`) plus the whole message page view.
- Reads run alongside the ongoing search.

**research_kind** (`:558-600`): `_usable` → `_search` → if nothing kept, one more `_search` with the `again` hint (or on a fresh tab after a stall) → wait for reads → `KindResult(kind, kept, records, seconds, stopped)`.

**Resolution** is mechanical: `resolve_mail()` (`:864-884`) → `valid_records` / `latest_per_key` / `_apply`.

**Budgets and limits**

| Limit | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Worker request limit | 20 (`UsageLimits(request_limit=max_steps)`), tool retries 4 | `research_mail.py:507`, `worker.py:187,213` |
| `KIND_SECONDS` | 150 s, when no `seconds` is passed | `research_mail.py:56` |
| Orchestrator per-kind budget | 120–240 s (`KIND_MIN_SECONDS` / `KIND_MAX_SECONDS`) | `orchestrator.py:62-63` |
| `MIN_KIND_SECONDS` | 50 s | `research_mail.py:57` |
| `STALL_SECONDS` | 45 s, then a fresh tab | `:58` |
| `KEEP_GRACE` | 60 s after the first kept hit, then the search is cut | `:59`, `:516` |
| `READ_RESERVE` | 25 s | `:60` |
| `RETRY_SECONDS` | 90 s | `:61` |
| `READ_TIMEOUT` / `PLAN_TIMEOUT` | 60 s / 30 s | `:62-63` |
| `MAX_VIEW` | 14,000 chars per page view | `browser_tools.py:24` |
| `MAX_RETURN` / `MAX_PAGES` (paging tool) | 30,000 chars / 40 pages | `research_tender.py:39-40` |

**Env switches**
- `MAIL_TABS` (default 6, `orchestrator.py:56`) and `AGENT_MAIL_SECONDS` (540, `:66`).
- `AGENT_FINDINGS_WAIT` (0, `:71`) and `AGENT_GAP_REWORK` (`:75`).
- `AGENT_CLEF` / `USE_CLEF` (`clef.py:30`).
- `LLM_TIMEOUT`, `LLM_TIMEOUT_THINKING`, `LLM_RETRIES`, `LLM_HEDGE_AFTER` (`llm.py:84-115`).
- There are no `MAIL_*` switches for thinking or batching. `llm.thinking(phase, default)` (`llm.py:738`, `THINKING_<PHASE>`) exists but is not wired into the mail search or reader.

## 2. Existing mechanisms

- **(a) One search, classify hits for several kinds in one call:** none. `Kind`, `_goal`, `_Reading` and `read_message` are all single-kind.
- **(b) Reuse a result list across kinds:** not by design.
  - `Collected()` is created fresh per `_search`.
  - Incidentally, `keep_results` matches against `session.seen`, which persists per tab across kinds. A later kind on the same tab can keep a link an earlier kind's list showed, but the model is never shown those earlier lists.
  - Nothing is shared between tabs.
- **(c) Several messages in one model call:** none. It is one `read_message` per kept view; `gaps.reread()` (`agent/gaps.py:471`) also calls it per view.
- **(d) A kind with thinking off:** no flag. `thinking=True` is hard-coded at `research_mail.py:507` (search) and `:373` (reader). The plumbing exists (`run_worker(thinking=...)`, `llm.thinking("…", default)`), so it would be a one-line switch.

## 3. `collect_pages` and pagination helpers

**`paging_tool(collected, thorough=False)` → `collect_pages(next_ref)`** (`research_tender.py:307-371`) is the one mail uses.
- The model names the next/load-more control. The helper clicks it up to 40 times, polling up to 4 × 0.7 s per page, and stores each full page view in `Collected.pages`.
- It returns the whole list as concatenated full page views (`=== page view i` plus the entire view, folders and chrome included), capped at 30,000 chars.
- These are raw views, not compact rows.

**Context retention** (`worker._forget_old_views`, `worker.py:87-108`)
- Only the latest view-bearing message is kept in full; older ones shrink to stubs.
- The `collect_pages` result contains `URL:\nTitle:` headers, so it counts as the latest view.
- The `keep_results` return has no such header (`_heads` joins with " / "). So after collect → keep, the collected text of up to 30k chars is re-sent in full on every later request until the model navigates to another folder.
- `collect_pages` is not in `KEEP_RESULTS = {"search","collect","extract"}` (`worker.py:60`), so it is stubbed entirely once a newer view arrives.

**`site_tools.paginate` / `search` / `collect`** (`site_tools.py:288-485`) are not used by mail.
- They return compact numbered rows (`ROW_CHARS` 300, `MAX_ROWS` 200, `MAX_PAGES` 25) with link targets.
- Their results stay in context up to `KEEP_CHARS` 12,000.
- Note that `keep_results` only finds links in `session.seen` in the `[eN link "text" -> href]` form, and `site_tools._format` rows use a different format (`["name" -> href]`), though `paginate` does run every page through `session.look()`.

## 4. Tests and dev scripts

**Unit tests** (offline, no model): run with `(cd agent && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests)`, or a single file with `uv run python -m unittest tests.test_research_mail`.
- `agent/tests/test_research_mail.py`: `MailDomainTest`, `KindBudgetTest` (`kind_budget`, approval-first), `ConversionTest` (fx, metal index, calc mapping), `SenderTest`, `SeveralKeysTest`, `LandedTest`.
- `agent/tests/test_orchestrator.py:277` `MailPlan` covers the `_plan_mail` quick-then-patient timeouts.
- `agent/tests/test_gaps.py` covers mail gaps and rework.
- `agent/tests/test_tender_qa.py:343-367` covers `resolve_mail` with reserves.
- Nothing tests `_goal`, `_search`, `keep_results`, `read_message` or `_forget_old_views` for mail.

**Dev scripts**: none of these is truly offline; they need the scouting logins and the model proxy.
- `dev/research_check_records.py [tender|mail]` is the mail-only harness. It runs `plan_searches` plus `research_mail.research_mail` and prints records and timings.
  - Run: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"; HEADLESS=1 MAIL_TABS=6 uv run --project agent python dev/research_check_records.py mail`
  - Its `MAIL_TABS` default is 5 and `CHECK_SECONDS` default is 600.
  - It uses `research_mail()`, not the orchestrator loop, so `KIND_SECONDS` 150 applies and there is no 120–240 s sharing.
- `dev/site_tools_check.py --mail-topic WORD --only mail` compares a mailbox search with and without `SITE_TOOLS`.
- `dev/local-soak.sh` and `dev/run-local.sh` do full local runs up to signing.
- `dev/research_check.py` is spec and ERP only.

## 5. Why one worker per kind

No comment or doc line explicitly warns against merging kinds. The design is described rather than argued:
- `research_mail.py:5-7`: "Per kind a worker (one tab each) chooses its searches and folders; `collect_pages` pages through a result list it points at and `keep_results` opens the hits whose subject it names (only links it has actually seen)."
- `orchestrator.py:54-55`: "about nine record kinds took three rounds over four tabs ... six tabs take them in two rounds (tabs are free, the work and its cost stay the same)."

Relevant warnings in `docs/learned.md`:
- `:250` "Mail search with thinking off took 211 calls instead of 85 and lost end_reserves in one run: keep thinking on."
- `:136-137` "One run with the mail kinds on site_tools.search/collect kept nothing in three kinds (150 s each; paging followed a message list into a session expiry); kept on the paging tool for now."

# Plan: cut cost x time toward 3rd place, staged and safe first

## Context

The public leaderboard ranks teams at quality 100 by cost x time. Third place (BaoByte) is at 3.9
($0.033 x 1:56). Our submission is at 49.7; the best recorded run of recent `main` is 19.3 ($0.097 x 3:19), which
would be 5th. No 2:20 run is in `experiments/runs.jsonl`, and 2:20 at today's cost would still be about 12.6.

Third needs roughly a third of today's cost and half the time together. A measured good run
(`run_c7403cf6df6fe24c`, 229 s, $0.090) spends them like this:

| Phase | Wall time | Cost share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research; the last mail kind ends it | 0-120 s | mail search 39 %, mail readers 11 %, ERP/spec ~30 % |
| Bid form after research | 120-201 s (80 s, only 5 model calls) | ~3 % |
| Review, TAN, submit | 201-228 s | small |

Decisions taken with the user: staged, low-risk cuts first; every change proven on public-1 (3 test runs at 100)
and on the evals (no drop); stop and report before any `atira submit`, since it replaces the final-run candidate.

Honest expectation: stage 1 lands around cost x time 10-13 (4th-5th). Stage 2 gets to roughly 6-8. Reaching under
3.9 needs stage 3 to work as well, and the teams ahead keep moving. Each stage is worth having on its own.

## Where the work goes

New branch `speed-cuts` off `main` (not `clef-on`: Clef adds calls and no points so far; it stays its own branch).
Carry over only the cache-share line in `llm.usage_table()` from `clef-on`, because it is used for measuring.
Commit per measured change, team conventions (author `josteng`, no trailers), no push without asking.

## Stage 1: low-risk cuts (no change to what the model decides)

Bid form and signing, `agent/submit.py`, `agent/configurator.py`, `agent/browser_tools.py`:

1. **Click that cannot crash the run.** `submit.py:454` clicks the next button outside the `try`; a covered button
   raised through the worker and restarted the whole form (seen on our synth portal). Give it the same fallback
   as `browser_tools._click` (overlay closed by the existing helper, then a JS click) and catch the timeout.
   Reliability first; this is the fix that turns a 0 into a signed bid on unfamiliar forms.
2. **Light settle inside the scripted position loop.** `configurator._confirm` (470-479) and
   `PositionDesk._enter` run a full `SiteSession.settle()` per cascade level: `networkidle` 2.5 s plus the
   login/cookies/error/human-check sweep. Add a light mode to `settle`/`_settle` (`browser_tools.py:487, 552`)
   that waits for the next control or a page change, and falls back to the full settle on any failure.
   Estimated 15-35 s of the 80 s.
3. **Drop duplicate looks.** `fill_position` returns its last view; `_enter` and `_continue` reuse it instead of
   calling `session.look()` again (`submit.py:348, 417, 443, 460`; `configurator.py:504`). Estimated 3-8 s.
4. **Shorter TAN round trip.** Add `fill_in` to the sign pass tools (`submit.py:757-758`) so TAN entry and submit
   are one model step, and start the mail reload in `request_signing_tan` (667) right after the click.
   Estimated 4-7 s.
5. **Warm mail tab.** `Mailbox` gets the same in-tab keepalive as `BidFlow._keep_alive` (934), so `_tan` reloads a
   signed-in inbox. Small typical gain, removes the 150 s tail noted in `docs/learned.md:215`.

Mail research, `agent/research_mail.py`, `agent/research_tender.py`, `agent/worker.py`:

6. **Compact result lists.** `collect_pages` (`research_tender.py:307-371`) returns up to 30,000 characters of raw
   page views that are re-sent on every later step. Return compact rows (subject, sender, date, link) in the
   `[eN link "..." -> href]` form that `keep_results` matches against `session.seen`.
7. **Batch the reader.** `read_message` (370-388) is one thinking call per kept message (14 calls, 11 % of cost).
   Read the messages kept by one `keep_results` call in one call returning a list of `MailRecord`, with the same
   grounding validator; `gaps.reread()` keeps the single-message path.
8. **End a search sooner.** Pass `notes=False` (the goal already forbids `note`/`back`), and stop the worker once
   each folder the mailbox shows has had a completed search, in the style of `ERP_DETAIL_STOP`
   (`_search`, 499-541; `KEEP_GRACE` at 516).

Not doing: thinking off for the mail search (`docs/learned.md:250`: 211 calls instead of 85 and a lost record).

## Stage 2: mail search covering several kinds (only if stage 1 holds 100)

One worker takes a small group of record kinds, searches the reference once per folder and calls
`keep_results(kind, link_texts)` per kind. Touches `_goal` (333), `_search`, `keep_messages_tool` (426),
`_Reading`, and the queue in `Orchestrator._research_mail` (`orchestrator.py:745-812`). Keep two or three groups on
separate tabs for parallelism and so one failed group cannot lose every record; rescale `KEEP_GRACE` and the
20-request cap. Behind a switch (`AGENT_MAIL_GROUPS`, default off until proven) so it can be compared and reverted.

Fair play: the model still chooses the query and folders and names which subjects belong to which kind. No helper
may sweep folders before a model call.

## Stage 3: only if stages 1 and 2 are proven and the gap to 3rd is still open

- ERP detail and spec readers (about 30 % of cost): same treatment as mail (compact views, fewer steps).
- Enter the on-screen position's material cascade as soon as materials are chosen, before prices. Needs a hook from
  `Orchestrator.select_materials` to `BidFlow`, a no-save mode in `_enter`, and partial entries past
  `configurator.complete_positions` (243). Riskiest item: unsaved state dies with the session and a choice can
  still change.

## Verification (per change, then per stage)

1. Unit tests: `(cd agent && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests)`; new cases beside
   `tests/test_auto_positions.py`, `tests/test_form_shapes.py`, `tests/test_signing.py`,
   `tests/test_research_mail.py` for the click fallback, light settle, batched reader and compact rows.
2. Offline form check: `dev/configurator_check.py` on the mock wizard; mail-only harness:
   `dev/research_check_records.py mail` (needs the scouting logins and `atira models proxy`).
3. Public-1: three `dev/test-run.sh v2 "<change>" <experiment>` runs; all three must score 100. Compare the
   phase times in the run summary and the per-caller table against `run_c7403cf6df6fe24c`.
4. Evals: `python3 dev/trainloop.py step "<change>"` with `dev/train_rules.json` listing `err404-synth-hazards-0`,
   `err404-traps`, `err404-layout`, `err404-nobid`; the reward must not drop against the `main` baseline step.
   Take the baseline step first. The platform has been failing eval runs on its side today; failed runs are not
   counted and are rerun.
5. Record every run (`experiments/runs.jsonl` via the dev scripts) and add a `docs/learned.md` bullet per result.

Run budget: 12 concurrent runs and 12 eval runs an hour are shared with the team; a full check is 3 test runs plus
4 eval runs, so coordinate before starting a round.

## Stop points

- After stage 1 and after stage 2: report quality, cost, time, cost x time and eval reward, and wait.
- No `atira submit` and no promotion of a test run without the team's confirmation.

Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.

   raised through the worker and restarted the whole form (seen on our synth portal). Give it the same fallback

   `PositionDesk._enter` run a full `SiteSession.settle()` per cascade level: `networkidle` 2.5 s plus the
   login/cookies/error/human-check sweep. Add a light mode to `settle`/`_settle` (`browser_tools.py:487, 552`)
   that waits for the next control or a page change, and falls back to the full settle on any failure.
   Estimated 15-35 s of the 80 s.
3. **Drop duplicate looks.** `fill_position` returns its last view; `_enter` and `_continue` reuse it instead of
   calling `session.look()` again (`submit.py:348, 417, 443, 460`; `configurator.py:504`). Estimated 3-8 s.
4. **Shorter TAN round trip.** Add `fill_in` to the sign pass tools (`submit.py:757-758`) so TAN entry and submit
   are one model step, and start the mail reload in `request_signing_tan` (667) right after the click.
   Estimated 4-7 s.

   signed-in inbox. Small typical gain, removes the 150 s tail noted in `docs/learned.md:215`.

   page views that are re-sent on every later step. Return compact rows (subject, sender, date, link) in the
   `[eN link "..." -> href]` form that `keep_results` matches against `session.seen`.

   grounding validator; `gaps.reread()` keeps the single-message path.

   each folder the mailbox shows has had a completed search, in the style of `ERP_DETAIL_STOP`

        """
        Tell, on a position page and without entering anything, which control takes which value, so the positions
        can be entered at once when the values are ready. `fields`: control label (exactly as in your view) ->
        value name. `confirm_button`: label of the button that applies a choice so the next choice opens.
        `next_button`: label of the button that saves the position and goes on (never one that omits or adds).
        """
        problems = mapping_problems(ctx.deps.session.view, fields or {}, self.known, (confirm_button, next_button))
        if problems:
            return "Not taken: " + "; ".join(problems) + ". Fix the mapping and call again."
        self.remember(fields, confirm_button, next_button)
        ctx.deps.session.trace.event(ctx.deps.session.name, "position_form_mapped", fields=self.plan.fields,
                                     confirm=self.plan.confirm, next=self.next_button)
        return "Mapping taken. Enter nothing on this page; return now."

    async def configure_position(self, ctx: RunContext[Deps], position: str, fields: dict[str, str] | None = None,
                                 confirm_button: str = "", next_button: str = "",
                                 choices: dict[str, str] | None = None, entered_yourself: bool = False) -> str:
        """
        Enter all values of the position the form shows now and, once all are in, save it and go on with the form's
        next/continue button. `position`: its number as the page shows it. `fields`: control label (exactly as in
        your view) -> value name; needed on the first call, later calls reuse it. `confirm_button`: label of the
        button that applies a choice so the next choice opens. `next_button`: label of the button that saves the
        position and goes on (never the one that omits or adds a position); needed once. `choices`: only when a
        call reported it: control label -> the option to choose. `entered_yourself`: True only after you entered
        a position yourself because this tool handed it to you.
        """
        session, plan, asked = ctx.deps.session, self.plan, position.strip()
        self.sync(session)

        def refuse(reason: str, text: str) -> str:  # every early return is traced: the run logs show why
            session.trace.event(session.name, "configure_refused", position=asked, reason=reason,
                                fields=fields or {}, text=text[:300])
            return text

        if entered_yourself:
            done = next((p for p in self.handed if p == asked or re.search(
                r"(?<![\w.])" + re.escape(p) + r"(?![\w]|\.\d)", asked)), None)
            if done is None:
                return refuse("not_handed", "Only a position this tool handed to you counts as entered by you; "
                                            "call configure_position() for the others.")
            self.entered.add(done)
            session.trace.event(session.name, "entered_by_model", position=done)
            return f"Position {done} counted as entered. {self.so_far(session)} Still to enter: {self.remaining()}."
        unknown = self.remember(fields, confirm_button, next_button)
        if unknown:
            return refuse("unknown_names", unknown)
        async with session.lock:
            view = await session.look()
            position, shown = resolve_position(asked, self.entries, view)
            if position is None or position not in shown:  # a page between two states: look again once settled
                await session.settle()
                view = await session.look()
                position, shown = resolve_position(asked, self.entries, view)
        if position is None:
            if shown:  # several of the bid's positions on one page: the model must name one of them
                return refuse("ambiguous", f"Name the position this page is about by its own number (one of "
                                           f"{', '.join(shown)}), then call again.")
            return refuse("no_values", f"No values for position {asked!r} (the page shows none of this bid's "
                                       f"positions {', '.join(sorted(self.entries, key=position_key))}): leave it "
                                       f"out with the form's option to omit a position. {self.so_far(session)}")
        if position not in shown:
            return refuse("not_on_page", f"Position {position} is not on the page now. Configure the position "
                                         "the page shows, by its own number; omit only a position that is not one "
                                         f"of {self.remaining()}.")
        if not plan.fields:
            return refuse("no_fields", f"Position {position} has values to enter. Give fields (control label -> "
                                       f"value name) for the controls of this form, then call again; do not omit it.")
        if position in self.handed:
            return refuse("handed", self.hand_over(position, session))
        if self.failures.get(position, 0) >= 3:
            return refuse("failed", f"Position {position} failed three times: leave it out with the form's option "
                                    f"to omit a position. {self.so_far(session)}")
        if time.monotonic() > self.deadline - self.reserve:
            return refuse("time", "Time is short: leave this and every remaining position out and go on to "
                                  "signing. " + self.so_far(session))
        entry = self.entries[position]
        values, labels = unmapped(view, entry, plan.fields)
        if values and labels and not self.asked_unmapped:  # asked once per run; the next call fills as mapped
            self.asked_unmapped = True
            return refuse("unmapped", f"Nothing entered yet. This bid has values for {', '.join(values)}, but no "
                                      f"control is mapped to them, while these fields of the page are not mapped: "
                                      f"{'; '.join(labels)}. Call again now with fields that add every one of them "
                                      "that takes such a value (the mapping you gave stays); leave out fields that "
                                      "match none.")
        self.layout = page_layout(view)
        text, saved = await self._enter(session, position, shown, asked, choices)
        if saved and AUTO_POSITIONS:
            text = await self._continue(session, text)
        return text

    def _auto_blocker(self, position: str | None, shown: list[str], view: str) -> str:
        """Why the next page is not entered with the mapping the model gave ('' when it can be): it must show
        exactly one bid position not yet entered, with the same controls (kinds and labels) as the position page the
        model named showed before it was filled, and time must be left."""
        if position is None or shown != [position]:
            return "the page shows no single bid position"
        if position in self.entered or position in self.handed or self.failures.get(position):
            return f"position {position} was entered or tried before"
        if not self.next_button:
            return "no save button named"
        if time.monotonic() > self.deadline - self.reserve:
            return "time"
        layout = page_layout(view)
        if layout != self.layout:
            return f"other controls: {sorted(layout ^ self.layout)[:6]}"
        return ""

    async def _continue(self, session, text: str) -> str:
        """
        After a position was entered and saved: the next position pages are entered with the same mapping as long
        as each one passes _auto_blocker; fill_position checks every option and value, and a failure or a page
        that does not pass goes back to the model with the latest result.
        """
        done: list[str] = []
        while True:
            async with session.lock:
                view = await session.look()
            position, shown = resolve_position("", self.entries, view)
            blocker = self._auto_blocker(position, shown, view)
            if blocker:
                session.trace.event(session.name, "auto_positions_stop", entered=done, reason=blocker[:200])
                break
            text, saved = await self._enter(session, position, shown, position, None)
            done.append(position)
            if not saved:
                break
        if not done:
            return text
        return f"Entered with the same mapping as well: {', '.join(done)}. " + text

    async def _enter(self, session, position: str, shown: list[str], asked: str,
                     choices: dict[str, str] | None) -> tuple[str, bool]:
        """Fill one position page and save it: the tool's message, and whether it was entered and saved."""
        plan, entry = self.plan, self.entries[position]
        async with session.lock:
            log: list[str] = []
            try:
                error = await fill_position(session, entry, plan, log, self.picks(position, entry, choices))
            except Exception as exc:  # a slow or changed page: the model decides to retry or omit
                error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc).splitlines()[0][:200]}"
            moved, saved = "", False
            if not error and self.next_button:  # the model named the button; clicking it is the mechanical part
                view = await session.look()
                ref, why = find_control(view, self.next_button, ("button",))
                target = await locate(session.page, ref) if ref else None
                target, own = await scoped(session, target, position)
                others = [p for p in shown if p != position and p not in self.entered]
                if target is None:
                    moved = f" Could not save it: {why}; click the form's next/continue button yourself."
                elif others and not own:  # the page's button would leave the other positions it lists unentered
                    moved = (f" This page also shows {', '.join(others)}: enter each with configure_position(); "
                             f"{self.next_button!r} is clicked after the last of them.")
                else:
                    await target.click(timeout=5000)
                    await session.settle()
                    moved = f" Saved with {self.next_button!r}; the page below is the form's next step."
                    saved = True
            session.trace.event(session.name, "configure_position", position=position, done=log, error=error,
                                moved=moved)
            view = await session.look()
        if error:
            self.failures[position] = self.failures.get(position, 0) + 1
            self.entered.discard(position)
            if NUMBER_ONLY not in error:  # the form, not the value, stood in the way
                self.form_failures[position] = self.form_failures.get(position, 0) + 1
            if self.form_failures.get(position, 0) >= HAND_OVER_AFTER:
                self.handed.add(position)
                session.trace.event(session.name, "handed_to_model", position=position, error=error[:300])
                return (f"Position {position} not entered: {error}. {self.hand_over(position, session)}\n\n{view}",
                        False)

    async def settle(self) -> None:
        """Let the page finish and run the generic helpers, but never longer than SETTLE_SECONDS: a click that never
        returns (seen on a cookie notice) must not block the tab for minutes. A page that answers no script call
        any more is opened again (reopen)."""
        alive = True
        try:
            alive = await asyncio.wait_for(self._settle_fresh(), SETTLE_SECONDS)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            self.events.append("the page kept loading; continuing with what it shows")
            self.trace.event(self.name, "helper_error", helper="settle", error=f"timeout after {SETTLE_SECONDS} s")
            alive = await self._answers() != "hung"
        if not alive and not self.starting:
            await self.reopen("the page answers no script call")

    async def _settle_fresh(self) -> bool:
        self.logins = 0  # a timeout later in the run may need a fresh sign-in
        return await self._settle()

    async def reopen(self, why: str) -> bool:
        """
        Give up a tab whose page stopped answering (run ec4e: the bid form hung for 8 minutes and every call into
        it waited out its timeout). The same URL opens in a new tab of the same context first: the site's session,
        and with it a server-side wizard's state, lives in the context's cookies. When that page does not answer
        either, the site starts again in a fresh context (signed in anew; what the old session held is gone, which
        `restarts` tells). True when a page answers again.
        """
        url = self.page.url if any(not p.is_closed() for p in self.pages) else self.site["url"]
        if not url.startswith("http"):
            url = self.site["url"]
        self.trace.event(self.name, "helper", action="reopen", why=why, url=url[:120])
        old, self.pages = list(self.pages), []
        for page in old:  # in the background: closing a hung tab may itself take a while
            asyncio.create_task(_close_quietly(page))
        try:
            page = await asyncio.wait_for(self.context.new_page(), STUCK_SECONDS)
            self._watch(page)
            try:
                await page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=GOTO_SECONDS * 1000)
            except Exception:
                pass  # still loading: whether it answers decides
            if await self._wait_answer(page):
                try:
                    await asyncio.wait_for(self._settle(), SETTLE_SECONDS)
                except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                    pass  # it answers; still loading is fine
                self.events.append("the page stopped answering; it was opened again in a new tab (check where the "
                                   "form stands)")
                return True
        except Exception as error:
            self.trace.event(self.name, "helper_error", helper="reopen", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"[:160])
        self.trace.event(self.name, "helper", action="restart", why="the reopened page does not answer either")
        await self._close_pages()
        self.restarts += 1
        try:
            fresh = await self._fresh_context("restart")
            if fresh is not None:
                self.context, self.scripted = fresh, None
            await self.start(attempts=2, until=time.monotonic() + START_SECONDS)
        except Exception as error:
            self.trace.event(self.name, "helper_error", helper="restart", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"[:160])
            return False
        self.events.append("the page stopped answering; the website was opened again from its start page and "
                           "signed in anew: steps not yet submitted are gone")
        return True

    async def _settle(self) -> bool:
        page = self.page
        for _ in range(6):
            try:
                await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", timeout=15000)
                await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle", timeout=2500)
            except Exception:
                pass
            if not await self._wait_answer(page):  # its helpers would hang on every page call
                self.trace.event(self.name, "helper_error", helper="settle",
                                 error=f"the page answers no script call ({page.url[:80]})")
                return False
            if (await self._safely(self._login, page) or await self._safely(self._cookies, page)
                    or await self._safely(self._error_page, page) or await self._safely(self._human_check, page)):
                page = self.page
                continue
            break
        await self._collect_closed(page)
        return True

    if kind == "combobox":
